outcomes.label: crashes harming a pedestrian
outcomes.description: Reported crashes in which at least one pedestrian was injured or killed, counted as events within 30 m of the corner.

outcomes.label: pedestrians injured or killed
outcomes.description: People on foot injured or killed, counted as people. One crash can injure several, so this is not a crash count. This is the unit NYC DOT reported.

outcomes.label: persons injured or killed, all modes
outcomes.description: Every person injured or killed, counted as people, including drivers and passengers as well as pedestrians and cyclists. This is the SECOND of the two outcomes NYC DOT reported, and it is not the same as a count of crashes in which somebody was hurt: one crash injuring three people contributes three here and one there.

outcomes.label: crashes in which any person was injured or killed
outcomes.description: Reported crashes in which at least one person of any party was injured or killed, counted as EVENTS rather than as people. NYC DOT did not report this outcome; its comparable outcome is total injuries above.

outcomes.label: all reported crashes
outcomes.description: Every reported crash, whether or not anybody was harmed, counted as events.

outcomes.label: vehicle to vehicle with a driver or passenger harmed
outcomes.description: Crashes recording two or more vehicles in which a driver or a passenger was harmed, which is the configuration a turning conflict moves.
